report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write in a news/headline/caption style (sensational, media-focused ledes), i.e., a headline/clickbait-esque news/entertainment summarizer.

Reasoning
- Lexical field strongly shifts toward news/media tokens and proper nouns: repeated “headline(s)”, “Driver”, “Sessions”, “van/von”, place/person names (“Manny”, “Royals”, “Vincent”, “Hunter”, “Malawi”, “Raipur”).
- Persistent, multi-layer convergence on headline-y, emotive adjectives across positions 2–4: “tragic”, “tragedy”, “iconic”, “vivid”, “timeless”, “colorful”, “vibrant”, “lush”, “loud”. These are hallmarks of headlines, photo captions, and culture/entertainment copy (“rocker”, “podcast”, “melodic”).
- Hard-news/disaster lexicon co-occurs: “victims”, “refugees”, “hurricane”, “law”, “leaders”, “alert”, “homes”, “windows”, reinforcing a newsroom domain bias.
- Sensationalist framing tokens appear: “worst”, “shocked”, “refused”, “blitz”, consistent with tabloid/clickbait style.
- Difference norms are maximal at the first token across many late layers (especially L25 p0 = 322), indicating the finetune strongly reorients the model’s opening tokens—exactly where headlines/ledes/captions matter most.

Together, these point to a finetune that makes the model default to producing news-style headlines or short captions/ledes with sensational, emotionally charged wording about events, people, and culture.
